title: Co-session hook bridge: delivery and enforcement for same-checkout coordination
summary: A host-agnostic bridge joins a co-session at session start, drains pending handoffs on each prompt turn, denies writes to foreign-leased paths, and releases leases at session end. Lease acquire/release are serialized by a shared inter-process lock. CLIs without lifecycle hooks poll the generic monitor instead.
hint_triggers: Pattern: keep all coordination logic in one neutral core (join/heartbeat/drain/lease-gate/end) and make each host a thin stdin/stdout adapter around its native hook events. Bind cleanup to the real session-end event, not a per-turn stop event. Identity derives from the host's stable session key (<provider>-<session_id>); when a host acquires a lease from its own CLI it must pass that id explicitly, since one-shot CLI processes fall back to a pid and the gate would deny the holder's own writes. Fail open everywhere except the affirmative lease deny; deny text names holder, expiry and alternatives. Wiring must be deliberate: a tracked settings file in the repo, or a generation ceremony for gitignored host state dirs — hand-installed configs drift silently.
